newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: World Bank denies recommending Argentine wage cuts.
newsitem.headline: World Bank denies recommending Argentine wage cuts.

text.p: A World Bank representative in Argentina on Tuesday denied newspaper reports that said it had recommended lowering local wages as a way to combat unemployment.
"Nowhere in our report do we recommend a drop in workers' salaries," Patricio Millan said in a World Bank statement.
"But we have recommended lowering taxes on labor and other levies that raise the cost of work," said Millan.
The Clarin newspaper said Monday that a World Bank report prescribed lower wages to bring down unemployment, currently at 17.1 percent.
Millan said labor reforms the government was trying to push through Congress are "essential to promote employment and reduce poverty."
On Monday, the government submitted a proposal to Congress seeking to change longstanding labor laws that it considers too rigid to foster job creation.
